keyVerseText: And of Asriel, the family of the Asrielites: and of Shechem, the family of the Shechemites:
rootMeaning: The root word אַשְׂרִיאֵל (ʼAsrîyʼêl), from which אַשְׂרִאֵלִי (ʼAsriʼêlîy) derives, literally means "I shall be prince of God." This patronymic indicates a descendant relationship to Asriel, a name borne by notable Israelites linked to the tribe of Manasseh. The literal sense of princely authority combined with divine association enriches the understanding of the Asrielites as not merely a family group but one connected to leadership under God's sovereignty.
usageInScripture: The term אַשְׂרִאֵלִי appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Numbers 26:31, where it designates the collective descendants of Asriel as a distinct clan. The consistent translation as "of the Asrielites" emphasizes their identity as a people group or family lineage, highlighting the tribal and genealogical structure foundational to Israelite society. This singular occurrence underscores the word's function as a precise ethnic and familial marker within the biblical narrative.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אַשְׂרִאֵלִי as the descendants of one whose name means "I shall be prince of God" invites reflection on God’s providential ordering of His people through appointed leaders and clans. It points to the divine purpose embedded in Israel’s tribal divisions, where each family’s identity carries theological weight. For the Christian faith, this reminds believers that God’s sovereignty extends over all human structures and histories, orchestrating lineage and leadership in fulfillment of His redemptive plan. The Asrielites, therefore, represent more than genealogy; they exemplify God’s faithful governance over His covenant people.
keyVerseReflection: Numbers 26:31 states, "And of Asriel, the family of the Asrielites: and of Shechem, the family of the Shechemites," marking the Asrielites as a distinct family within Israel’s census. The use of אַשְׂרִאֵלִי here highlights the importance of preserving the identity and heritage of each clan under God’s covenant. This designation not only records genealogical data but also affirms God’s ongoing relationship with His people through their familial lines, reminding us that every group within Israel has a purposeful place in His divine plan.
